WHAT KIBU DOES

Everyday chores, done through the files and apps you already use.

Ask in plain words.
Kibu does the work.

  • Files.

    Find a file, organize a folder or rename a batch. Preview changes and undo them.

    Try sayingOrganize my Downloads folder

  • Your day.

    Manage Calendar, Reminders and Notes. Draft emails for you to review and send.

    Try sayingRemind me to call mom tomorrow at 7

  • The web.

    Read pages and work through sites. Kibu asks before sending, posting or buying.

    Try sayingSummarize this page

  • Other apps.

    Work with windows, buttons and selected text through macOS Accessibility.

    Try sayingExplain the error I just selected

  • Remember and remind.

    Keep notes, tasks and focus timers close. Memories stay on your Mac.

    Try sayingStart a 25 minute focus timer

  • And it’s a pet.

    Drag Kibu around, drop files on it, or let it dance and nap. Tuck it away whenever you need.

    Open it from anywhere⌥ Option Space

YOU STAY IN CHARGE

Kibu acts when you ask, and only then.

Little helper.
Your call.

See the plan.

Kibu previews file changes before anything moves.

Pause or stop.

Pause, resume or stop any task. ⌘⇧Esc stops Kibu at once.

Changed your mind?

Moves, renames and new folders can be put back. So can new events, reminders and notes.

Hands off your mouse.

Kibu never moves your pointer or types for you. If something needs a click, it tells you what to click.

Nothing sent without you.

Mail stays a draft, and Kibu asks before anything that sends, posts or buys.

Limits on every task.

A step limit, a time limit and a spending limit, checked before each step.

BRING YOUR OWN AGENT

Kibu is the hands. The agent is the head.

Kibu needs an agent
to think with.

Connect Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or an Anthropic API key for open-ended tasks. Choose during setup; change it any time.

  • A coding agent on your Mac. Kibu detects Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode and uses your existing login.
  • Or an Anthropic API key. Pay Anthropic per use. Your key is encrypted with your macOS Keychain.
  • The agent only proposes. Kibu’s own code checks every step against what you have allowed before anything runs.
  • No agent yet? Finding, tidying and renaming files, reminders, calendar, notes and timers still work without one.
INSTALL

Early release, version 0.1. Built on your Mac, from source.

One line in Terminal.
Kibu does the rest.

A Mac
Apple silicon, M1 or later. Intel Macs are not supported.
macOS
14 Sonoma or later.
Node.js
Version 22 or later, from nodejs.org.
Apple’s tools
The command line tools. If you don’t have them, run xcode-select --install first.
An agent
Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or an Anthropic API key. Why Kibu needs one.
Terminal
git clone https://github.com/madhurjyadc/kibu.git && cd kibu && npm install && npm run app
  1. It builds Kibu.app. The command builds the app on your Mac, puts it in Applications and opens it.
  2. Kibu shows you around. A one-minute tour, one permission at a time. Nothing is requested until you tap Allow.
  3. Press ⌥ Space. Kibu opens from anywhere. You can also click its face in the menu bar.

To update, run git pull && npm install && npm run app in your kibu folder. Full instructions in the README on GitHub.

PERMISSIONS AND PRIVACY

You decide what Kibu can reach, one permission at a time.

Your Mac.
Your permissions.

What Kibu asks for
  • Desktop, Documents and Downloads to find, tidy and rename files.
  • Calendar, Reminders, Notes and Mail to help with your day.
  • Your browser to read the page you’re on: Safari, Chrome, Arc, Brave or Edge.
  • Accessibility and Screen Recording to read windows and press buttons in other apps.
  • Notifications for reminders and timers.
What Kibu keeps private
  • Everything is saved locally. Tasks, history and memories live in a database on your Mac.
  • Only what a step needs is sent to the agent you chose. Kibu uses cloud models, so it is not an offline app.
  • No snooping. Kibu does not index your files or take continuous screenshots.
  • Some places are off limits. System folders, SSH keys and your Keychain cannot be opened, even if asked.
  • No secrets in memory. Kibu refuses to remember passwords, codes, keys and card numbers.

QUESTIONS

The short answers. The long ones are in the README.

Before you install.

Which Macs does Kibu run on?

Macs with Apple silicon (M1 or later) running macOS 14 Sonoma or later. Intel Macs, Windows and Linux are not supported.

What does “needs an agent” mean?

Kibu does the work on your Mac, but the thinking comes from an AI agent you already have: Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode on your Mac, or an Anthropic API key. Without one, Kibu still handles files, reminders, calendar, notes and timers, but it cannot take on open-ended requests.

What does it cost?

Kibu has no price, no account and no subscription. With Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode it uses the plan you already have. With an Anthropic API key, Anthropic bills you for what you use, and each task stops at $1.50 unless you change the limit.

Is there a .dmg I can download?

Not yet. For now you build Kibu from source with one command. An app built on your own Mac opens without a security warning from macOS, and you can read every line of it first.

Will Kibu take over my mouse or keyboard?

No. Kibu never moves your pointer or types for you. It works through files, app scripting and macOS Accessibility, and if something can only be done by clicking, it tells you what to click.

Can it send email or buy things for me?

Not on its own. Mail only ever becomes a draft for you to send, and Kibu asks before anything that sends, posts or buys.

Where does my data go?

Your tasks, history and memories stay in a local database on your Mac. Kibu uses cloud models, so it is not an offline app: the context a step needs is sent to the agent you chose, and nothing else.

How do I update or remove it?

To update, run git pull && npm install && npm run app in the kibu folder. To remove it, quit Kibu and delete Kibu.app from Applications. Its data lives in ~/Library/Application Support/Kibu.

Is Kibu finished?

No. This is an early release, version 0.1, so expect rough edges. The repository lists exactly what has been tested and what has not.
